title: Solve scheduler priority-inversion causing intermittent cold-start stalls across Hosted/Dedicated/Private
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: Multiple customers across Hosted, Dedicated and Private reported intermittent request stalls that present as long cold-starts (10s-30s) for short interactive queries when mixed with heavy long-context batching traffic.

Symptoms:
- Short requests (<=512 tokens) observe multi-second stalls intermittently (not constant).
- Occurs under mixed workloads: a minority of long-context streaming requests (>=8192 tokens) plus many short interactive calls.
- Affected environments: hosted ap-southeast, dedicated GPU pools with mixed tenant routing, and one private on-prem deployment (customer CT-1150).
- Customer escalations: CT-1123, CT-1150, CT-1168.

Investigation notes:
- Initial triage by SE showed per-worker request queue growth then stall. Grafana traces show request stuck in scheduler queue with no worker assignment.
- Scheduler logs indicate a priority-inversion pattern: a large batched inflight work item (long-context) holds a worker and prevents the scheduler from rotating in urgent short requests; the queue aging logic failed to bump priority quickly enough.
- Reproducer created in staging: synthetic mix 80% short, 20% long; batching window=5ms, preemption disabled, KV cache cold. Observed tail stalls within 5-15 minutes.
- Root cause hypothesis: when batched long requests occupy critical worker slots, the scheduler's fairness counter and aging heuristic undercounts short-request urgency during bursty arrivals. Additionally, KV cache warmup for long contexts triggers heavyweight memory churn that delays worker readiness events, amplifying stalls.

Decision and design summary:
1) Short-term hotfix (low risk): implement request "aging" that increments effective priority every 50ms while queued, capped at one level above normal. Also add a soft preemption check that allows a short request to be inserted into a worker if batch-growth is below threshold.
2) Medium-term fix: fair-share tokens per-route and bounded preemption that avoids breaking model correctness for streaming long-contexts.
3) Long-term: scheduler refactor to support multi-tenant cooperative preemption and KV cache pinning for interactive sessions.

Patch implemented in branch: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2145 (see links). Hotfix changes: aging window, soft preemption, and a KV-cache warmup backoff to reduce eviction thrash.

Rollout plan:
- Canary in Hosted (us-east-1) with 5% traffic for 6 hours, then 20% for 12 hours.
- If metrics stable, expand to Dedicated staging pools and notify top affected Dedicated customers to join canary.
- Private customers will be given the patch and migration guide; provide assisted rollout for CT-1150.

Monitoring and metrics to observe post-rollout:
- Scheduler queue depth distribution (p50/p95/p99).
- Median and 99th short-request cold-start latency.
- Worker busy fraction and KV cache miss rate.
- Customer error rates for CT-1123/1150/1168.

Rollback plan: revert branch and re-enable previous scheduler config; dial batching window up to 15ms to reduce churn.

Notes on customer communication:
- Sent interim update to CT-1123 and CT-1150 on 2025-02-13 with mitigation steps.
- Postmortem will include timeline, root cause, and long-term mitigations; expected to publish by 2025-03-05.
acceptance_criteria: Short-request p99 cold-start latency reduced to <2s under mixed workloads in staging
No increase in error rate or model correctness regressions after preemption change
Canary rollout across hosted does not regress CPU/GPU utilization beyond 5%
Affected customers confirm reduced stalls in Dedicated/Private environments
